guide.summary: Forgejo documents an OAuth2 authorization-code provider (with PKCE) for user-consented access, and the connected person's token acts as that user. OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token is not limited to repository listing or read-only access.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List repository names visible to the connected person, with pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: OAuth2 authorization code flow is documented for third-party apps
findings.detail: Forgejo acts as an OAuth2 provider with user consent. It supports the Authorization Code Grant with PKCE and confidential or public client types. Apps are registered in user settings.
findings.appliesWhen: The customer connects an individual account on their own Forgejo instance using OAuth.

evidence.quote: Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:

OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

findings.title: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented; the token boundary is the user's full access
findings.detail: OAuth2 tokens can execute any action on behalf of the user, not only Git actions. Third-party apps that obtain a token through this flow receive administrative rights. Read-only behavior must be enforced by the app, not by the token.
findings.appliesWhen: Any OAuth token issued for this app, including the connected person's token.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Note Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to
Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.

findings.title: Register the OAuth app in the customer's own instance settings before testing
findings.detail: Registration is done through the user settings applications section, which is required before the authorization code flow can be tested.
findings.appliesWhen: The customer uses OAuth on their own instance.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.

steps.title: Register the OAuth2 application on the customer's Forgejo instance
steps.detail: Register an OAuth2 application in the instance user settings (/user/settings/applications) with a redirect URI supplied by the customer. Use a confidential client for server-side apps or a public client with PKCE for native apps. Record the Client ID and Client Secret (secret shown once). Customer provides the instance base URL, which must be used as <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>; the documentation host forgejo.org is not used for API calls.
steps.doneWhen: The application appears in the user's applications list and the Client ID and client type are recorded for the test.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.

fields: <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>: customer-provided full HTTPS base URL of their Forgejo instance
<CLIENT_ID>: from the registered application
<CLIENT_SECRET>: from the registered application (confidential clients only)

steps.title: Open the authorization URL and verify the callback
steps.detail: Redirect the customer to the instance authorization endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and a random state. The customer must approve the request. On approval Forgejo redirects to the redirect_uri with code and state; verify the returned state matches the sent value before exchanging the code. The token will act with the full rights of the connected user because OAuth2 scopes are not implemented.
steps.doneWhen: The callback URL contains a code and the matching state value.

evidence.quote: https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an application in the settings. The STATE is a random string that will be
sent back to your application after the user authorizes. The state parameter is optional but should be used to prevent CSRF attacks.
The user will now be asked to authorize your application. If they authorize it, the user will be redirected to the REDIRECT_URL , for example:

fields: <REDIRECT_URI>: the redirect URI registered for the application
<RANDOM_STATE>: random string generated by the test app
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: POST the returned code to the token endpoint with the same redirect_uri used in the authorization request. Confidential clients send client_secret; public PKCE clients send code_verifier instead. This is an unexecuted authorization step; the response contains access_token used as a bearer token for the API requests.
steps.doneWhen: The response includes access_token, token_type bearer and expires_in.

evidence.quote: POST https://[YOUR-FORGEJO-URL]/login/oauth/access_token { "client_id" : "YOUR_CLIENT_ID" ,

Response: { "access_token" : "eyJhbGciOiJIUzUxMiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJnbnQiOjIsInR0IjowLCJleHAiOjE1NTUxNzk5MTIsImlhdCI6MTU1NTE3NjMxMn0.0-iFsAwBtxuckA0sNZ6QpBQmywVPz129u75vOM7wPJecw5wqGyBkmstfJHAjEOqrAf_V5Z-1QYeCh_Cz4RiKug" ,
Use the access_token to make API requests to access the user’s resources.

fields: <RETURNED_CODE>: the code value from the callback URL
<CLIENT_SECRET>: confidential clients only; public PKCE clients use code_verifier instead
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: List visible repository names, first page
steps.detail: Send a GET request to the repository search endpoint with private=true, which includes private repositories the connected user can access, plus limit and page=1. limit sets page size. Read names from $.data[].name, where $ is the top-level response object, data is the collection of repository objects, and name is the string property of each element. Use the name property, not full_name. Confirm the top-level ok property is true. Representative input: private=true, limit=50, page=1. Use the access_token from the code exchange as a Bearer token and the user's HTTPS instance base URL without a trailing slash. Boundary check: this request must be GET only; confirm the outgoing request log contains no create, edit or delete calls.
steps.doneWhen: The response has ok true and names are read from data[].name; the response headers are checked for a Link header with rel=next. Boundary check: with the same token, confirm the outgoing request log contains only this GET to the repository search endpoint and no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE calls.

evidence.quote: ## GET /api/v1/repos/search | Search for repositories
Parameter private in query (boolean, optional): include private repositories this user has access to (defaults to true)
Response JSON paths for GET /api/v1/repos/search: $.data[].name (string)

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
ACCESS_TOKEN: access_token from the code exchange response
private=true: include private repositories the user can access (documented default)
limit: page size; use the documented value from settings API

steps.title: Boundary check: confirm the response is read-only and token scope is user-wide
steps.detail: Use a documented excluded read to confirm private visibility is determined by the connected user, not by a grant. Inspect the actual OAuth grant and outgoing request log to confirm only GET requests are sent by the test app. Do not attempt a write request.
steps.doneWhen: Only GET requests appear in the outgoing request log and the grant shows the user-wide access documented for OAuth2.

Access Token Scope Forgejo supports scoped access tokens, which allow users to restrict tokens to operate only on selected URL routes. Scopes are grouped by high-level API routes, and further
Parameter private in query (boolean, optional): include private repositories this user has access to (defaults to true)

fields: private=false: restricts results to public repositories for comparison
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
Access token: backend OAuth exchange for the test account; keep it out of this guide

steps.title: List visible repository names, continue until no next link
steps.detail: Repeat the same search with private=true and the same limit, incrementing page by one each time (2, 3, and so on). Continue until a response's Link header has no rel=next entry; that is the documented end of pagination. Do not treat an empty data array as the stopping rule. If a Link header with rel=next is returned, follow that URL unchanged rather than constructing a cursor. The x-total-count header gives the total item count and can be used to cross-check the total read. Collect data[].name from every page. Boundary check: this request must be GET only; confirm the outgoing request log contains no create, edit or delete calls.
steps.doneWhen: Stop only when a response has no Link header entry with rel=next, as documented for pagination; the collected names cover every page. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to the repository search endpoint and no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE calls.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
< link: < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search ? limit = 1 &page = 2 > ; rel = "next", < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search? limit = 1 &page = 5252 > ; rel = "last"
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.

fields: page: incremented by one from the previous request until no rel=next link
limit: same value as the first request
ACCESS_TOKEN: same token from the code exchange
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

details.title: OAuth2 authorization code flow is documented for third-party apps
details.detail: Forgejo acts as an OAuth2 provider with user consent. It supports the Authorization Code Grant with PKCE and confidential or public client types. Apps are registered in user settings.
details.appliesWhen: The customer connects an individual account on their own Forgejo instance using OAuth.

evidence.quote: Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:

OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

details.title: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented; the token boundary is the user's full access
details.detail: OAuth2 tokens can execute any action on behalf of the user, not only Git actions. Third-party apps that obtain a token through this flow receive administrative rights. Read-only behavior must be enforced by the app, not by the token.
details.appliesWhen: Any OAuth token issued for this app, including the connected person's token.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register the OAuth2 application on the customer's Forgejo instance
Register an OAuth2 application in the instance user settings (/user/settings/applications) with a redirect URI supplied by the customer. Use a confidential client for server-side apps or a public client with PKCE for native apps. Record the Client ID and Client Secret (secret shown once). Customer provides the instance base URL, which must be used as <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>; the documentation host forgejo.org is not used for API calls.
Fields: <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>: customer-provided full HTTPS base URL of their Forgejo instance, <CLIENT_ID>: from the registered application, <CLIENT_SECRET>: from the registered application (confidential clients only)

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Open the authorization URL and verify the callback
Done when: The callback URL contains a code and the matching state value.

Exchange the authorization code for an access token
Done when: The response includes access_token, token_type bearer and expires_in.

List visible repository names, first page
Done when: The response has ok true and names are read from data[].name; the response headers are checked for a Link header with rel=next. Boundary check: with the same token, confirm the outgoing request log contains only this GET to the repository search endpoint and no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE calls.

Boundary check: confirm the response is read-only and token scope is user-wide
Done when: Only GET requests appear in the outgoing request log and the grant shows the user-wide access documented for OAuth2.

List visible repository names, continue until no next link
Done when: Stop only when a response has no Link header entry with rel=next, as documented for pagination; the collected names cover every page. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to the repository search endpoint and no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE calls.
